finding.claim: Unauthenticated GET /rss fetches an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL with no scheme, host, IP, or port validation and returns the first 400 bytes of the response to the caller, enabling non-blind SSRF to internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints.

trace.note: Route is unauthenticated; params[:u] is attacker-controlled.
params[:u] passed directly to URI.open. A string containing a scheme (e.g. http://) is parsed by open-uri and fetched over the network, with no check on host or address.
First 400 bytes of the fetched body are returned in the HTTP response, so the attacker reads the internal response.

finding.guards_checked: None on the path. No allowlist on host, scheme, IP range (RFC1918, loopback, 169.254.169.254), or port. No check on the redirect target: open-uri follows redirects, so an allowed external host can 302 to an internal address. The TRUSTED constant (app.rb:5) is defined but never used on this route. Note: a non-URL string with no scheme falls through to Kernel#open, which is a separate local-file and pipe issue outside SSRF scope.

verdict.reason: The `/rss` route at app.rb:7 takes `params[:u]` with no authentication, passes it unvalidated to `URI.open` at app.rb:8, and returns the first 400 bytes of the response at app.rb:9, so the attacker reads the fetched body. The only host check in the file, `TRUSTED` at app.rb:5, is used only by `/trusted` at app.rb:14, not by `/rss`.

finding.claim: Route /trusted's host allowlist is enforced correctly for SSRF purposes, so it is not reported. Its only residual weakness is that the allowlist does not constrain port or scheme, which would let a caller reach any port on the allowed hosts. That is low impact and not a finding.

trace.note: Same URI object is parsed once and used for both the check and the request.

uri.host is compared by exact membership in TRUSTED. Userinfo tricks (http://feeds.example.net@169.254.169.254/) parse with host=169.254.169.254 and are rejected. Backslash and whitespace inputs raise InvalidURIError instead of passing.
Net::HTTP.get does not follow redirects, so no post-check redirect bypass exists.

finding.guards_checked: Exact host membership against TRUSTED (app.rb:14), validation and request use the same parsed URI object (app.rb:13,15), and no redirect following. Not reported: no port or scheme restriction, which is low impact on allowed hosts.

verdict.guard_found: app.rb:14 `halt 400, "no" unless TRUSTED.include?(uri.host)`: exact set membership on the parsed hostname, and the same `uri` object is passed to `Net::HTTP.get(uri)` at app.rb:15, so the request host is the checked host.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled `params[:u]` (app.rb:13) is parsed once and must have `uri.host` exactly equal to `feeds.example.net` or `news.example.net` (app.rb:14) before `Net::HTTP.get(uri)` runs (app.rb:15), which is a closing exact-host guard; the candidate's trace lines match the code. The residual port/scheme looseness is outside the SSRF finding criteria, so this is not reportable as an SSRF.
